column3: Lays out the area grid: splits the area width and height by the column and row weights and sets up the scrollbar. \n It writes the area index into the owner widget (`+0x7c`, if there is one; and clears `+0xbe9`) and clears the first visible widget. Outside grid-only areas (flag `0x80000`), when there are columns and rows, it computes the margins (flag 1: 0; otherwise 2 at the sides and, at top and bottom, 2 with flag `0x10` or a single row, 8 for the others), turns on the scrollbar (`0x403600`) when the widgets exceed the rows, and splits the width and the height by the weights. \n More than 30 columns or rows: the original routine runs (error box, `Area.cpp 497` and `507`).

Initialises the area: rectangle clamped to the screen, fields, cleared scrollbar and the column and row weights. \n An area that opens on top of a widget (`dono` ≠ -1): weight 1 in all 30 columns and rows, zero rectangle, 1 column and 0 rows. For the others: it orders x1/x2 and y1/y2 (swap `0x90ba90`), x1/y1 at least 0 and x2/y2 at most the screen (`0x31f`/`0x257` in the 800x600 exe; the 1920x1080 exe replaces these immediates, which are read here from the exe itself). It writes the fields, clears the scrollbar and, outside grid-only areas (`0x80000`), copies the weights (with 1..29 columns/rows and a pointer) or fills them with 1 (also with 30 or more: in that case the original overruns the 30-entry array, and so does this code). The visible rows are clamped at 30 (the grid size); the rest goes to the scrollbar.

Draws the area: the panel, the grid lines or each visible widget in its cell, and the scrollbar. \n With `redesenhar`, it frees the saved image (`0x5e42b0`); an area that opens on top of a widget saves the background (`0x5e3dd0`); it draws the panel (`0x5e5df0`). Grid-only area (`0x80000`): the grid lines (`0x5e3730`, colour `[0xae317e]`) and that is all. For the others: it saves the scrollbar background, places each visible widget in its cell (the grids `+0x1c`/`+0x10c` and `+0x94`/`+0x184`, when the widget has no rectangle of its own at `+0x28`/`+0x30`) and draws it (`0x5ee590`) until it passes the last row; then the scrollbar (`0x403c80`). \n Without a first visible widget (`+0xb76` = -1): the original routine runs (error box `Area.cpp 245` and the layout `0x403350`).

Creates the fixture of a tie (or only marks it as deferred): competition, round, rules, clubs, date (tomorrow if already past), slot, stadium and calendar; the news to human managers; in a two-legged round, the second leg `+0x22` days later with home and away swapped. 
 Convention: thiscall, ret `0xc`, `Cup.cpp`, SEH frame with no destructor on the normal path (the local dates and news item). `Cup::create_tie_fixtures(rodada, confronto, adiar)` (round, tie, defer), called from the round set-up (`0x51c800`) and from the competition screen. 
 Tie −1: the first tie of the round with flag `+0x34` = 1 (defer) or 2 (create); none: 0. Defer: flag 2. Create: flag 3; with a team missing (`+0/+2` = −1), the news of the pending tie (`0x522950`: push tie; push round; mov ecx, esi -> thiscall, ret 8). 
 Otherwise the fixture is built in a local of `0x4f` bytes: the competition (`+0x14`) and the id (`+0`, −1 if none), −1 at `+8`, the cup year (`+0x40`) at `+0x2c`, `+0x3a` at `+0x32`; from the round (`0x68` bytes at `+0xa3`) the code `+7` (`+3` in a two-legged round, `+0x21` = 2) at `+0x30`, `+9` at `+0x34`, `+0xb` at `+0x36`, the rules `+0xd` at `+0x38` (with no second leg and with `0x800`: `0x1000` if the level (`+4` of the team) of the home team is not lower than the away team's, otherwise `0x800`), `+0x17` at `+0x3a`; the league (`+0x44`) at `+0x42`, the flags (`0xff`, 1, 0), the cup's virtual `+0x7c` (push &fixture; mov ecx, esi), bit `0x400` of `+0x4d` (no second leg and `+0x20` > 0), the clubs (`+0x1c`, `+0x20`) and ids (`+0xc`, `+0x10`; −1 with no club), the date (day `+3`, year `+5` + the cup's), the slot `+6`, the date of the next round (`+0x6b`/`+0x6d`; 0 in the last one), the stadium (`0x85c260`: push `+0x24` of the cup; push &fixture; push `+0x13`; mov ecx, `[0xdd7ef4]` -> thiscall, ret `0xc`) and the calendar (add_fixture_to_calendar). 
 With a human manager at either club and without bit `0x100` in `+0xd`, news item `0x14` goes to both. In a two-legged round, with the cup still in `[0xadadfc]`: the second leg `+0x22` days later (`0x549ef0`, `0x54c5b0`, `0x417c10`), code `+4`, the slot by the day of the week (`0x54a3f0`: Saturday or Sunday 1, otherwise 2), home and away swapped, the stadium and the calendar. Returns 1.

Posts news item `0x26` for a tie with an undecided team: the cup, the round and the possible teams, to the managers of each club. 
 Convention: thiscall, ret 8, `Cup.cpp`, SEH frame with no destructor on the normal path (the local news item). `Cup::post_draw_news(rodada, confronto)` (round, tie), called only from `0x51cb90`. 
 With both teams decided, or a round (`0x68` bytes at `+0xa3`) with fewer than 2 ties (`+0x1a`): nothing. Each side with no team (`+0/+2` = −1) comes from its source tie (round `+0xe/+0x10`, tie `+0xa/+0xc`; with no source or with a team missing there: nothing): the two possible clubs; with a team, its club (`+0xa7`, 6 bytes). 
 News item `0x26`: 0 = the cup id, 1 = `+0x3a`, 2 = the round code (`+7`), 3/4 = the home team and −1 or the two possible ones, 5/6 = the away team and −1 or the two possible ones; sent to the managers of each of its clubs (`0x7861e0`: push club; push &news; mov ecx, `[0xb7431c]` -> thiscall, ret 8; the possible ones only if not null).

The round draw by seeding (round rule `0x400`): the teams leave the ties, are sorted by seed (highest first), and each goes to a drawn tie. 
 `Cup::sort_round_teams(rodada)`. 
 1) It takes the teams out of the ties into an array of 7-byte entries (malloc `0x944e46` of 7 × slots `+0x18`; out of memory, the box of line `0xbf8` and the game stops), each with its seed (`+4` of the team). 2) Sorts by seed, highest first (qsort `0x945333` with `0x51ebc0`). 3) Each entry with a team (up to the first without one, level `0xff`) goes to a drawn tie (`0x90cfc0` over the ties), moving round in a circle: on the first pass, only ties with both slots empty (< 0): with both free (−2), the drawn side (`0x90cfc0(2)` ≠ 0: home); only home free: home; only away free: away. From the second pass on (the flag is never reset to zero), any free slot, but with round rule 4 (`+0xb`) a free home slot is not allowed when the away team of the tie is from the same nation, and a free away slot is not allowed when the home team is; after going all the way round again, the nation rule is dropped (also for the following entries) and, without it, the box of line `0xcff` and it exits. 
 Frees the array (`0x9452ca`).

The round draw that keeps nations apart (round rule 4 without `0x400`): each team's level becomes how many teams of its nation are in the round (the bigger nations go first) and, from the second pass on, a team does not land in a tie with another of its nation while possible. 
 `Cup::check_round_teams_for_nation(rodada)`. 
 It counts the teams of each nation in a zeroed array of `[0xae2350]` bytes (`0x945501`; out of memory, the box of line `0xd27` and the game stops) while taking the teams out of the ties (malloc of 7 × slots, the box of line `0xd34`), using `+0` of the club's nation (`+0x53`); the level of each entry with a team becomes its nation's count (with no nation, the seed stays); it frees the counts and sorts, highest first (the nations with more teams go first). 
 Each entry (up to the first with `0xff`) goes to a drawn tie, in a circle: on the first pass, only ties with no team in either slot (with both free, the drawn side; with only one free, that one); from the second on (the flag stays), any free slot, except (while the rule holds, and it is restored for each entry) a tie with a team of the same nation as the entry's club; after going all the way round again, the rule is dropped and, without it, the box of line `0xe5c` and it exits. Frees the array.

Pays the round prize money: the winner gets the news item and the money, the loser only the money; the fund loses both. 
 `Cup::pay_round_prize_money(vencedor, perdedor, rodada, partida)` (winner, loser, round, fixture; 6-byte entries of the two teams). 
 The round prizes are `+0x60` (winner) and `+0x64` (loser); with −1 for the winner, the fund (`+0x28`) / (rounds `+0x3c` − round) / ties (`+0x1a`), and with −1 for the loser as well, 3/4 to the winner and 1/4 to the loser. 
 The winner (if the prize is not zero) gets the news item (`0x48e3e0`: the team's outcome `+5`, 3 if it was 1 in fixture `0x136`, and the next round: its word `+7` if it is neither the last nor `0x8c`, over the high 16 bits of the round pointer, as the original leaves in ebp) and the money (`0x5999a0` on the finances `0x5a0590`); the loser only the money; the fund loses both.

Swaps home and away in one tie or in every tie of the round by the round rule: the club in the higher division (virtual `+0x90`), the team level or the cup stadium. \n `Cup::set_home_teams_for_round(rodada, laco)` (round, tie): in one tie (`laco`) or in all those of the round (−1), with both teams decided (≠ −1), it swaps home and away by the round rule (low byte of `+0xb`): bit 1, if virtual `+0x90` (club_in_higher_division(club a, club b)) returns club b; otherwise bit 8, if the level (`+4` of the team, signed) of a is lower than b's; otherwise, with the cup stadium (`+0x24`) ≠ −1, if club b exists, has a stadium (`+0x69`) and its id (`+0`) is the cup's.

Records how far the team went in the cup, by outcome and round (with or without a third-place round), through virtual `+0x68` (`set_club_progress(clube, competição +0x44, p1, p2, p3)`, i.e. club, competition `+0x44`, p1, p2, p3). 
 `Cup::record_team_progress(time, rodada)` (team, round). 
 With a last round of type `0x8c` (third place): in the semi-final (rounds − 2), outcome 1 or 2 → (d, d, d); in the last one, 3 or 4 → (d, d, d); in another round, outcome ≠ 0 → the round's `+0x5b` three times; 0 → (4, 1, 4) before the semi-final, otherwise (x, 1, x) with `+0x5b` of the next round. 
 Without it: in the final, 1 → (1, 1, 1), 2 → the ties (`+0x1a`) of the final + 1 three times; in another round, outcome ≠ 0 → `+0x5b` three times; 0 → (x, 1, x) with the ties + 1 of the final before it, otherwise `+0x5b` of the next round. Outcomes other than these call nothing.

Draws a cup round: with some team still open it puts the draw off by 1 day; otherwise it draws by the round rule, sets the home teams and the shared stadium, marks the drawn ties and sends the draw news to human-managed teams. Returns 1. 
 Convention: thiscall, ret 4, `Cup.cpp`, SEH frame with no destructor on the normal path. `Cup::draw_round(rodada)`. 
 Without `+0x45` or with the round already drawn (`+0x34` of the first tie): nothing. With a team of some tie still without a club: the draw date moves 1 day (`0x54c5b0`, `0x417c10`) and those of the following rounds become at least that date. 
 Otherwise it draws: rule `0x400` (`+0xd`) by seeding (`0x51d2d0`), rule 4 (`+0xb`) keeping nations apart (`0x51d9f0`), without `0x200` the open draw (`0x51e220`); the home teams (`0x51e870` with −1); shared stadium (`+0x21` = 2, `0x522610`); marks the drawn ties (`+0x34` = 1). 
 With news (skips_draw_news): a round that is not the third-place one (`+7` ≠ `0x8c`) adds 1 to `+0xac`; news item `0x27` (the competition, `+0x3a`, the type, `+0x44`, the round, 0, and 1 if `+0xab` + 1 < `+0xac`) goes to each of the teams still alive (outcome 0) among the first ones (sum of the entries `+0x1c` of the rounds up to this one) that has a human manager, with the manager's id in data item 3.

Updates the staff records by the club's outcome in the cup: the winners record (and the UEFA Cup place through the English League Cup or a European nation's main cup), runners-up, third place, qualified for the next round or knocked out, weighted by round. Returns 0. 
 Convention: thiscall, ret `0x18`, `Cup.cpp`; virtual `+0x44` of the English cups and of the base class. `Cup::update_staff_records_for_status(clube, desfecho, _, _, jogo, final)` (club, outcome, _, _, fixture, final). 
 Nothing with fixture `+0x3a` = 1, with `+0x2c` or with `+0x44` ≠ `0xff`. Outcome 1: the winners record and, with the place (wins_uefa_cup_place), the club's state receives the UEFA Cup (`[0x9cf6f0]`); 2: runners-up; 3: third place; 0: if the next round (`+0x34` + 1) exists and is not the third-place one (`+7` ≠ `0x8c`), the qualification (`0x86bdd0`) with weight round × 99 / (rounds − 1) + 1; `0xff`: the knock-out (`0x86c000`) with weight round × 99 / rounds + 1. 
 The stage records take the dwords the original pushes: the word of the fixture (`+0x32`, `+0x30`) or of the round (`+7`) over the high 16 bits of the register.

Records the season honours: finds the winner, runner-up, third (in the Welsh cup, through the statistics) and the host national team, writes the history row and, in the nation's main cup, passes the semi-final losers to UEFA. \n Convention: thiscall, ret 0, `Cup.cpp`; virtual `+0x30` of the English cups and of the base class. `Cup::record_season_honours()`: the history row (`0x4afce0`: 5 pushes; add esp, `0x14` -> cdecl(cup, winner, runner-up, third, host)) with the four from season_honours; outside the friendly competition, in the nation's main cup (is_main_national_cup), the semi-finalists go to UEFA (`0x519fc0`: ecx = the cup -> thiscall, ret 0).

Finds the semi-finals (`0x82`) and the final (`0x96`) and sends the two semi-finalists not in the final to the UEFA seeding. \n `Cup::register_semi_final_losers_for_uefa()`: the semi-finalists outside the final (semi_final_losers) go to the UEFA seeding (`0x905790`: push b; push a; push competition id; ecx = `[0xde1f58]`; no add esp -> thiscall, ret `0xc`).

Appends to the output the clubs that can still play the fixture, walking down the fixtures the empty sides come from. \n `Cup::collect_possible_teams(rodada, jogo, saida, *conta)` (round, fixture, output, *count). \n Null output or count: the original routine runs (the error box).

Returns the club on one side of the fixture or, if that side is empty, the clubs that can still reach it. \n `Cup::get_fixture_side_teams(rodada, jogo, lado, saida)` (round, fixture, side, output): the club on one side of the fixture (side ≠ 0: `+0`; 0: `+2`) or, if empty, the clubs that can reach it (`0x5219b0` with the count in global `0xae1880`). Returns the count (the error box if none). \n Round outside 0..`+0x3c`, a cup with no clubs (`+0xa7`) or fixture −1: the original routine runs (the error box and 0).

The daily update of each cup: moves on completed stages and ends the cup, gives each stage the day and, on the date, draws (phase 0) or sets up (phase ≠ 0) the rounds until none advances. Returns 0. 
 `Cup::update_for_date(hoje, fase)` (today, phase). 
 A cup with no parent (`+0x44` = `0xff`): with `+0xb1`, if stages 0..=`+0x30` are complete (virtual `+0x10` with 0, 1), it moves to the next stage (virtual `+0x28`, if `+0x30` < `+0x2c` − 1) or ends the cup once (`+0x4c`: the history `0x442e80` of `[0xad9da8]`, virtual `+0x30`, the records `0x4a19f0` of Comp_Stats `+8`); then the records news (`0x4a2450`). Still with no parent, each stage receives the day (virtual `+0x14` with `0xae2c90` and the phase). 
 Phase 0 (with `[0xae2c88]` = 1): the last, final round (`+7` = `0x8c`) is drawn on its date (`0x51c410`); without `+0xb1`, it draws the rounds from `+0xac` whose date has arrived, until none advances or they run out. Phase ≠ 0 (with `+0x45`): the same with the round set-up (`0x51c800`) from `+0xab`, which also sets up on the round's pending date (`+0x34` of the round's stage).

Sets up a cup round: draws the round if needed, creates the fixtures of the marked ties, moves them to the round dates and moves on; a team without a club postpones the rounds by a day. 
 `Cup::set_up_round(rodada)`: without `+0x45`: 1. Round outside 0..`+0x3c` − 1: the error box (line `0xa64`) and −1. It draws the round if its stage has no `+0x34` (`0x51c410`). 
 In the current round (`+0xab`): if a tie (`0x35` bytes in the stage, `+0/+2` the teams or `0xffff`) has a team without a club (`+0xa7`, 6 bytes), it postpones the requested round and the following ones by a day (`0x54c5b0`, `0x417c10`; the following ones only if they ended up earlier) and returns 1. 
 Otherwise it creates the fixtures of each marked tie (`+0x34` = 1 deferred, 2 already: `0x51cb90`; after the 2, without the cup in `[0xadadfc][id]`: 1), moves the fixtures to the round dates (date `+3/+5` in an 8-byte block, `0x51ebe0`, freed afterwards) and, with the cup in `[0xadadfc][id]`, moves on to the next round (except the final `0x8c`) and takes `+0xac` along. Returns 1.

The open draw of the round's teams: takes the teams out of the round ties, shuffles them and puts each one in a drawn tie (empty ones first), drawing the side when both slots are free, and sets the link to the next round. 
 `Cup::randomize_round_teams(rodada)`. 
 1) It takes the teams out of the ties (`+0x1a` of the round) into an array of 7 bytes per slot (malloc of 7 × slots `+0x18`; out of memory, box of line `0xe7f` and the game stops): the home team (`+0`, with the link `+0xe/+0xa`) and the away team (`+2`, with `+0x10/+0xc`), each with the team level (`+4` of the team); the tie slot becomes −2 (free); with no team (−1), the entry stays −1 (with `0xff` in the level). 
 2) Shuffles: for each position, swaps with the entry drawn among all of them (`0x90cfc0(n)`). 
 3) Each entry with a team goes to a drawn tie (`0x90cfc0` over the ties), moving round in a circle: on the first pass only ties with both slots empty (< 0); then any with a free slot (−2); after going all the way round on the second pass, box of line `0xf4c` and it exits (the second-pass flag is never reset to zero). With both slots free, it draws the side (`0x90cfc0(2)`: ≠ 0 home). The team carries its link (`+0xe/+0xa` or `+0x10/+0xc`) and, with a link, the tie of the next round receives the round (`+0x12`), the drawn tie (`+6`) and the side (`+8`: 1 home, 0 away). 
 Frees the array (`0x9452ca`).

Swaps home and away in the later tie whose team shares a stadium with a team of an earlier tie of the round, and sets the side in the linked ties. \n `Cup::separate_shared_stadium_ties(rodada)`: for each tie `i` of the round, it looks for the first `j > i` whose home team (or, failing that, the away team) shares the stadium (`+0x69` of the club, not null) with the home (or the away) team of `i`; if found, it swaps tie `j` (home and away, `+0xa/+0xc` and `+0xe/+0x10`) and fixes the side (`+8`) of the linked ties in the next round: the one at `+0xe/+0xa` becomes 1 (home), the one at `+0x10/+0xc` becomes 0. The two fixtures in the same stadium no longer fall on the same side.

qsort comparer of the cup entries by level (`+4`), highest first; on a tie, by club reputation (`+0x80`), lowest first. \n `cup_compare_entries_by_level_desc(a, b)`: the qsort of the cup entries (draws of the UEFA Cup, the Intertoto and the cups of Japan and Scotland). Hot (called by qsort): no counter.

Decides who goes through in a cup match (1 home, 2 away, 0 nobody) by the rule (`+0x38`), storing each side's code (`+0x3d`/`+0x3e`). \n `Cup::decide_fixture_winner(jogo)` (fixture): by the score (`+0x43`/`+0x44`), extra time (bit 2, `+0x47`/`+0x48`), penalties (bits `0x21`, `+0x49`/`+0x4a`), the walkover (`0x800`/`0x1000`) and the points (`0x2000`: codes −1 and the seeded team). The code of each side (`+0x3d`/`+0x3e`): 2 won, 3 in extra time, 4/5 on penalties, 8 walkover; −3 with `0x2000`. \n Null fixture or a draw on penalties: the original routine runs ("Error" box).

Decides a two-legged tie: in the first leg it marks the winner and returns 3; in the second leg it decides by aggregate, walkover, extra time, away goals and penalties (1 or 2 the side through, 4 undecided). 
 Convention: thiscall, ret 8, `Cup.cpp`; `this` is not read. `Cup::decide_tie_winner(confronto, jogo)` (tie, fixture): in the first leg (`+0x33` ≠ 1), it only marks the winner (points `0x10`: code 1; `0x2000`: −3, or −1 for both) and returns 3. 
 In the second leg, by the aggregate (`+0x14` + `+0x1f` against `+0x1e` + `+0x15`): 2 if the first side is ahead, 1 the second; level: walkover (`0x800`/`0x1000`, code 8), extra time (bit 2 with `+0x22` ≠ `0xff`: with `0x4000` the away goals in it; code 6, otherwise the extra-time difference, code 3), away goals (without 4 or `0x4000`, code 6) and penalties (`0x21`, `+0x24`/`+0x25`: code 4 with bit 1, otherwise 5); nothing decided: 4. Points (`0x10`) and rule `0x2000` have their own branches. 
 A draw on penalties: the original routine runs ("Error" box, 4).

Copies the round rules onto the match and, with a decision on a draw, marks who goes through by both sides' levels. \n It passes the rules of the match's round (word `+0xf` of round `[jogo+0x34]`) to the match flags (`+0x38`, OR). With flag `0x800` (decides who goes through on a draw), the level (byte `+4` of the slot, signed) of the two sides of tie `chave` decides: home team lower removes `0x800` and sets `0x1000`; higher keeps `0x800`; equal removes `0x800` and sets 1.

Returns the tie of the match's round (`+0x34`) that holds the match's home club (`+0xc`), or -1 if none. \n It looks at both sides of each tie (53 bytes; a negative slot is empty). The number of ties is word `+0x1a` of the round. Null match: the original routine runs (error box).

Returns the cup match importance by round and the first-leg score difference. \n The importance is the match stage `+0x34` minus `+0x3c` plus the cup's `+0x51`, at least 1; in `margem` it puts the first-leg score difference (`+0x4b`/`+0x4c`, `0xff` with no first leg) for side `segundo`, plus 1 (`0xff` below 1). Returns only `al`.

Outside friendlies, calls the competition's virtual `+0x44` and posts news item `0x10` about the team's result (club, competition, outcome, result category, the match, the next round), delivered by scope, to the competition region (final and third-place match) or to the club manager. \n Convention: thiscall, ret `0x14`, `Cup.cpp`, SEH frame with no destructor. `Cup::add_team_result_news(clube, desfecho, a3, partida, a5)` (club, outcome, a3, match, a5): friendly (`0x5c6710`), 0. The competition's virtual `+0x44` (`[0xadadfc]` by the id at `+4`) with the club, the outcome, a3, the output (`0xff`), the match and a5; −1 from it or no match: 0. \n News item `0x10` (local): 0 the club, 1 the competition, 2 the outcome, 3 the result category (`0x4b0890`), 4 what the virtual returned, the match from data item 5 on (`0x4afeb0`, which advances the cursor) and at the cursor the next round (`+7` of round `+0x34` + 1, up to `+0x3c` − 1; `0x8c` or outside: −1). Output ≠ `0xff`: delivery by scope (`0x786090`). Outcome 1 in round `0x96` or 3 in `0x8c` (`+0x30`): to the competition region (`0x786860`); otherwise to the club manager (`0x7861e0`). Returns 1.

Tells whether the cup is complete: it has started (`+0xb1`) and, when asked for the stages with no stage set (`+0x44`), all stages up to the current one are complete and the current one is the last. \n `Cup::check_complete(fases, _)` (stages, _): 0 if the cup has not started (`+0xb1`). With `fases` = 1 and no stage set (`+0x44` = `0xff`): each stage from 0 up to the current one (`+0x30`, array `+0xc`) must be complete (method `+0x10` with 0, 1) and the current one must be the last (`+0x2c` − 1); otherwise 0. Apart from that, 1.

In rounds with set dates, moves each round fixture to the weekday and time slot of its match-day slot, with the news, the stadium and the calendar; the used slot becomes empty. 
 Convention: thiscall, ret 8, `Cup.cpp`, SEH frame with no destructor on the normal path (the local news items, date and list). `Cup::move_round_fixtures_to_set_dates(data, rodada)` (date, round), called from the round set-up (`0x51c800`, in Rust). The local news item `0x14` is built right away (`0x77bbe0`).

With no stadium or on neutral ground: average × factor. 
 Derby (`+0xb3`/`+0xb7`/`+0xbb`): ×1.5 (same city ×1.35); rival away side ×1.35; off neutral ground with `+0x3b` != `0xff` ×1.05 and ×0.85. In the league with `+0x6d`: the minimum by the number of clubs in the league (and the maximum with up to 4 clubs). A stadium with fewer than 1,500 seats becomes R × 1,000 (at least 1,500). Limits by capacity (the away side up to max(5%, min(capacity − away average × home factor, 15%)) and the home side the rest; neutral half), with no stadium 40,000 and 25,000; with no crowd, 1 to 50 and 1 to 15. 
 Total = home + away − random(50) (negative: 45 to 194).

Scores a venue for a neutral fixture: the English national stadium before 2004 scores 0; the score starts at 100000, changes with the city distances (flag 8) or with the seats against the expected crowd (flag `0x20`) or becomes random(seats) (flag 4), and ends × (random(100) × 0.004 + 0.8). 
 `Stadium::score_venue_for_fixture(estadio, marcas, casa, fora, jogo)` (stadium, flags, home, away, match), called by the neutral venue search `0x85c800` (with flags `0x20` in career matches). The English national stadium (nation `[0x9cf2e4]` `+0x80`) before 2004: 0. 
 The score starts at 100000: flags & 8, with the cities of both clubs (`+0x69` → `+0x38`) and the stadium's (`+0x38`) and more than 10000 seats (`+0x3c`): by the distances d1 (home-away), d2 (home-stadium), d3 (away-stadium): with d1 < 30, 200000/180000/140000 if d2 and d3 < 15/30/50 and 50000 if either exceeds 100; otherwise 200000 if both < 0.588·d1 and 50000 if either ≥ 0.8333·d1. 
 flags & `0x20`: the expected crowd (10000; home national team 60000; otherwise the sum of the crowds `+0x73` of both clubs, at least 5000 and, above 40000, half of it without going below either of the two); seats above it: × 1.2; above 1.5× it: / ((seats − 1.5·expected)·8.33e-5 + 1); below 0.3/0.5/0.7/0.9 of it: × 0.1/0.3/0.7/0.9. 
 Otherwise, with flags & 4: the score is random(seats). At the end, score × (random(100) × 0.004 + 0.8), truncated.

Returns the travel distance factor for the attendance: 1 − distance × k (squared without `+0x3c`), divided by (reputation + 1)² when far and with reputation, with several minimums. Returns the double in st0. \n `Stadium::get_travel_distance_factor(jogo, cidade_do_estadio, cidade_do_clube, base)` (match, stadium city, club city, base), in the match attendance (`0x85cba0`, called by the engine `0x6b7f20`). D = distance between the cities (halved with match `+0x30` = `0xa0` and `+0x3a` = 5); F = 1 − D·`[0x96afe0]`, squared without `+0x3c`; with D and the reputation R (byte `+0x7e` of nation `+0x53` of the away club `+0x20`) above `[0x9689a0]`: F / (R + 1)². \n With base above `[0x969558]`, the minimum 1 − (`[0x968ea8]` − base)·`[0x968f20]`; with `+0x3a` = 10, the minimum 0.2; with both clubs of the same nation, 0.05; and always `[0x96d2c8]`.

The stadium daily update: on day 0 it rebuilds the venue list; before 2003 it closes the England national stadium and reopens it on 1/6/2003 with 90000 seats; every 30 days it removes the expired bookings and re-sorts. \n `Stadium::daily_update(hoje)` (today), every day from the game's day loop (`[0xdd7ef4]`). On day 0 of the year it rebuilds the venue list (`0x85dfc0`). Before 2003, the England national stadium (nation `+0x80`) closes: the id goes to `[0xa835a4]`, the nation and the senior national team (`+0x69`) are left without a stadium. On 1/6/2003 (`0x549f70`) it comes back with 90000 seats (`+0x3c`, `+0x40`). \n Every 30 days, the bookings (list at `+0`, count at `+4`, 12 bytes: id and date) before today are removed: the original counts the first k (year unsigned, day signed), copies over them, moving forward, the k that start at n − k − 1 (not at n − k) and re-sorts the n − k (`0x945333` with `0x85e380`).

Appends a booking (stadium id and date) to the list, which grows 30 at a time, and re-sorts by date and id. \n `Stadium::add_booking(estadio, data)` (stadium, date): appends the booking (stadium id, copy of the date via `0x417c10`) to the list (`+0`; count `+4`, capacity `+8`), which starts with 30 (`0x944e46`, `0x168` bytes) and grows 30 at a time (`0x945667`), and re-sorts (`0x945333` with `0x85e380`). Null stadium or date, or out of memory: the "Error" box (lines `0x810`, `0x81b`, `0x82b`). Called by the venue choice (`0x85c260`, `0x85c800`).

Returns 1 when there is no booking of the stadium on the date. \n `Stadium::is_stadium_free_on_date(estadio, data)` (stadium, date): 1 with no booking list; otherwise 1 if the binary search (`0x946464` with `0x85e380`) does not find the booking (stadium id, date copied via `0x417c10`). Called by the neutral venue choice (`0x85c800`).

Rebuilds the list of venues for neutral-ground matches (finals and semi-finals): grounds with a city, nation and continent qualify, except the City of Manchester Stadium (under construction) and, in nations with competitions, those under 5000 seats; each nation's national stadium is flagged. \n `Stadium::build_venue_list`: `+0xc` the list of 16-byte records, `+0x10` the count, `+0x14` the capacity; the old list is released. The hosts of the next editions of three competitions (keys `0x9cf79c`, `0x9cf7a4`, `0x9cf7ac`; `0x5fa7d0` on HostCountry `[0xb5e134]`, without it the box of line `0x858`) are found, but change nothing (their loop ends the same way on both paths). \n The stadiums that go in (records of `0x4e` bytes in `[0xae23b0]`, count `[0xae2358]`) are those with a city (`+0x38`), the city's nation (`+0x1f`) and the nation's continent (`+0x71`), except the "City of Manchester Stadium" (still under construction in 2001) and, in nations with competitions (`+0x11c`), those with fewer than 5000 seats (`+0x3c`). Each record: `+0` the nation id, `+4` the continent id, `+8` whether it is the national stadium (`+0x80` of the nation), `+0xc` the stadium. The list grows 30 at a time (`0x944e46`, realloc `0x945667`; out of memory, the boxes of lines `0x89c` and `0x8ac`, and it stops). At the end it is sorted (qsort with `0x85e2f0`) and `+0x18` = 1.

In a national team match, the people of that team's nation in the nation index (binary search by nation) serve one match of their ban under rule 0, one by one from a list of their ids (the count can release the ban and reorder the index). \n Convention: thiscall, ret 4, `discipline.cpp`, SEH frame for the local LLIST (`0x68d020`/`0x68d040`). `Discipline::serve_international_bans(time)` (team), called by the national team match (`0x7e8090`, in the ruling body of the bans). The people of the team's nation in the nation index (nation_index_range) go into a list (`0x68d0d0` with the item and 4: a copy of the id, because the count can release the ban and reorder the index) and, for each one, one match served under rule 0 (`0x556e90` with 0 and 1). At the end the list is destroyed.

Applies the result of a ban appeal: the ruling body drops the person's pending bans; a match ban loses matches (or stops at the counter) and a timed ban loses days, and it is released when over or when the appeal lifts it. \n `Discipline::apply_appeal_result(id, regra, reduz, menos_jogos, menos_dias, novo, dias_fixo, _)` (id, rule, reduce, fewer matches, fewer days, new, fixed days, _), called by the appeal result (`0x6abf99`, the human manager's news). With the person's entry in the ruling body (`0x7e82e0` without creating) and a ban (`+6`): the body removes the person's pending bans (`0x7e91d0`); by matches (`+0` ≠ `0xff`): `novo` ≠ `0xff` removes `novo` matches (below 0: zero and release), otherwise `reduz` removes `menos_jogos` and releases if it ends at or below the counter (`+1`), otherwise releases; by days: `dias_fixo` ≠ −1 removes `menos_dias` (down to 0: zero and release), otherwise `reduz` removes and releases at 0, otherwise releases. Release: `0x556d00` with the index.

Returns the text of the ban in the person's slot, from the ruling body of its rule; with no rule in the slot, 0. \n `Discipline::get_slot_text(pessoa, vaga, saída, tamanho)` (person, slot, output, size), called by the person screen (`0x87618a`, with `0xc8`). A person with id from `[0xae2364]` on: 0. The slot's rule (ban_slot_rule) `0xff`: 0; otherwise its ruling body's text (`[[this] + 4 × rule]`, `0x7e88d0` with the person, the output and the size). Null person: the original routine runs (it reads the id from 0).

Adds a ban: when the person already has a ban under one of the 4 rules, extends the old one (matches or days) and flags both; otherwise copies the new ban into the array's first free slot (or the end, growing by 100 up to `0x7d00`), links each rule to it and, with the fourth rule, adds {id, nation} to the nation index. \n `Discipline::add_ban(id, suspensao)` (id, ban): if any of the 4 rules of the new ban (`+0xc..+0xf`) already has a ban for the person (the body's entry with `+6` > −1), it extends the old one (matches `+0` added together or, with either of the two by days (`0xff`), the days `+2`) and flags both (`+0x13` bit 0); otherwise (bit 0 of the new one cleared for each rule with no ban) it copies the new one (`0x556c70`) into the first free slot of the array (`+0` = `0xff` and `+2` = −1), or at the end (count `+0xa`, capacity `+8`; grows by 100, up to `0x7d00`, malloc/realloc, the new slots free), links each rule to the index (`0x7e8510`) and, with the fourth rule, puts {id, nation} into the nation index (`+0xc`, capacity `+0x10`, count `+0x12`; grows by 20; qsort `0x55e5f0`). "Error" boxes (capacity at maximum, out of memory) via show_error_at.

When a loan ends, puts the person's held bans back into their slots (freeing the occupied slot first; the item leaves the list) and frees slots 0..2 not restored whose ruling body does not cover the contract club. \n `Discipline::restore_held_bans(pessoa)` (person), at the end of a loan (`0x4d07e0`): the contract (`0x4cf5a0`, stored in `[0xae1080]`) gives the club; for each held ban of the person in list `[this+0x1c]` (id, slot `+4`, the 5 bytes `+5`), while there are held bans (`+0x1c` of the record, signed): the occupied slot is freed first (the ban released, `0x556d00`), the held ban goes back to the slot, leaves the list (`0x68d1f0`, which frees it) and the count drops. Then the slots 0..2 not restored (never the fourth: the original's `k != 3`) whose ruling body does not cover the club are freed.

Releases a ban: each ruling body of the ban's 4 rules forgets it; on the fourth rule, the person's item leaves the nation index; the ban becomes free. Returns the ban. \n `Discipline::release_ban(id, indice)` (id, index): ban `indice` (20 bytes in `[this+4]`; the word is signed): for each of the 4 rules (`+0xc..+0xf`, `0xff` = none), the ruling body forgets it (`0x7e8590`); on the fourth, the person's item leaves the nation index (the last one is moved into its place, count `+0x12` − 1, qsort `0x945333` with `0x55e5f0`; if not found, "Error" box and it carries on). Finally the ban becomes free (`+0` = `0xff`, `+2` = −1).

Clears the person's ban history: the last entry of the history is dropped (`+0x18` of the 29-byte record = −1, via `0x58f110`). \n `Discipline::clear_ban_history(pessoa)` (person): the person's ban history (29-byte record of the id in `[this+0x14]`) loses its last entry (`0x58f110` on `[this+0x18]`: `+0x18` = −1). Returns what `0x58f110` returns. Null person or not a player (`+0x61`): the original routine runs (fatal box).

Copies a ban record (`0x14` bytes): the fields, the date (`+4`) and bits 0..2 of `+0x13`. Returns `this`. \n `BanRecord::operator=`: copies the ban record from `origem` (source): `+0` and `+1` (bytes), `+2` (word), the date at `+4` (`0x417c10`, return value in a local), `+0xc..+0xf` (byte by byte), `+0x10` (byte), `+0x11` (word) and bits 0..2 of `+0x13` (the other bits are kept).

Tells whether the player is suspended: by the general ruling body (`0x7e85b0` with 1) or by the competition's (`+0x50`, with 0); in the latter case, at a human-managed club, he leaves his slot among the 20 at `+0x1e0`. \n `Discipline::is_player_suspended(jogador, competição, extra, partida)` (player, competition, extra, match): player outside the people (`[0xae2364]`) or a non-existent competition (id in `*comp`, array `[0xadadfc]`): 0. Suspended by the general body (`[[this]]`, `0x7e85b0` with 1): 1. Otherwise, by the competition's body (`+0x50`, ≠ −1, with 0): 1, and if his club (`+0x39`) is human-managed (`0x600a50` with 0, 1, 0, 0), he leaves the slot he holds among the 20 at `+0x1e0`. Otherwise 0.

Removes the person's items from the held-ban list (`+0x1c`) while the `+0x1c` counter of the person's record is positive. \n `Discipline::drop_held_bans(pessoa)` (person): from the list of held bans (`+0x1c`; the cursor `+0xa` goes back to the start `+2`), it removes (`0x68d1f0`) each item of id `*pessoa` while the counter of the person's record (`+0x1c`, signed) is positive, decrementing it for each item.

Holds bans for a loan: the bans (slots 0 to 2) that do not apply at the loan club go to the held list (`+0x1c`), the slot becomes −1 and the `+0x1c` counter goes up. \n `Discipline::hold_bans_for_loan(jogador)` (player): with the player's contract sheet (`0x4cf6d0` on `[0xae1050]`), each ban in his record (slots 0 to 2) that does not apply at the loan club goes to the list of held bans (`+0x1c`, `0x68d0d0` with 10 bytes: the id, the slot and its 5 bytes), the slot becomes −1 and the record's `+0x1c` counter goes up. No contract sheet: the original routine runs ("Error" box).

Tells whether the person is one booking away from a ban: with a valid id, it asks the competition's ruling body; otherwise 0. \n `Discipline::is_one_booking_from_ban(pessoa, competicao)` (person, competition): with a valid id, the competition (`[[0xadadfc] + 4 × id]`) and its ruling body (`+0x50`, `0xff` if none; `[this]` + 4 × body), the question to the body (`0x7e8d60` with the id, 0, 0 and the competition's `+4`); otherwise 0. Called by the club screen (`0x4849f0`).

Processes a match for discipline: the competition's ruling body judges it; without one, in friendlies, the league ruling bodies of both clubs. \n `Discipline::process_match(partida, resultado)` (match, result): the ruling body of the match's competition (`+0`, id > −1) judges it (`0x7e7ff0` with 1, 1, 1). Without one, in a friendly (`0x5c6710` on `[0xae2c74]` with `+0x14`) or in competition `[0x9cf684]`: the league (`+0x57`) body of the home club (`+0x1c`, with 1, 0, 0) and that of the away club (`+0x20`, with 0, 1, 0). Returns what the first body returns (the other paths, 0; nobody reads it).

Removes a player from discipline: clears the ban history, releases the bans and frees the 4 slots, drops the held bans from the list and leaves the 29-byte record free (`0xff`, count 0). \n `Discipline::remove_player(id)`, called by the regen (`0x7abac0`): deletes the ban history (`0x55e1d0`), frees the 4 slots of the 29-byte record (with an entry in the ruling body: the ban released, `0x556d00`, the slot free and entry `+0` = −1), removes the person's held bans from list `[this+0x1c]` (`0x68d1f0`, while count `+0x1c` > 0) and the record becomes `0xff` with count 0.

Returns the player's held ban in a slot, or 0 if none. \n The held ban of player `id` in slot `vaga`: it walks the list of held bans (`+0x1c`, from the start, `0x68d1b0`) while the player has any (byte `+0x1c` of the 29-byte record in `[+0x14]`) and returns the one with the same player and slot.

Returns the tactic block (`0x1ecd` bytes) of the active slot of the human manager's record. \n `HUMAN_MANAGER::get_active_tactic(tecnico)` (manager), called by the team selection (`0x6db500`), the formation (`0x6e0230`), the match day (`0x6b4360`), the club tactic (`0x896660`) and the screens. The tactic block of the active slot (signed byte at `+0x9a69` of the record) of the manager (null: the current human). No manager or out of range: the original routine runs ("Error" box, 0).

Selects the human manager's active tactic slot: 4 for the second national team, 3 with reserve in a national team, 2 in a national team, 1 with reserve, 0 for the first team. \n `HUMAN_MANAGER::select_tactic_slot(reserva, clube, tecnico)` (reserve, club, manager), by the same callers as `0x5fbd00`. Null manager: the current human (with none, nothing); null club: the manager's (`+0x39`). The active slot (`+0x9a69` of the record): 4 in the second national team (`0x5409b0`), 3 with `reserva` in a national team (`0x53b900`), 2 in a national team, 1 with `reserva`, 0 in the first team. Out of range: the original routine runs ("Error" box).

Clears (79 bytes) the watched fixture of each active human manager who may no longer watch it. Returns 1. \n `HUMAN_MANAGER::clear_invalid_watched_fixtures()`: for each of the 16 human managers (the last 16 of `[0xae23bc]`) that is active (`+0x5f` ≠ 0) and can no longer watch his watched fixture (`0x5fe700`), it zeroes its 79 bytes.

Tells whether any of the active human managers chose to watch the fixture. \n 1 if any of the 16 active human managers (110-byte records in `[0xae23bc]`, from `[0xae2364]` − 16, `+0x5f` not zero) chose to watch `partida` (`0x5fe290`); otherwise 0. Null fixture: the original routine runs (error box and 0).

Tells whether the human manager (or the current one) gave the person a nickname, by binary search in his list. \n 1 if human manager `humano` (0 = the current one) gave a nickname to the person with id [`pessoa`]: binary search (`0x946464` with `0x601a10`, items of `0x1e` bytes) in list `+0xa6e3` (count at `+0xa6eb`) of his record (`0xa6ef` bytes in `[this]`). Null person or human, or empty list: 0. Human out of range: the original routine runs (error box and 0).

Tells whether the fixture is the one the human manager chose to watch. \n Whether `partida` is the one the human chose to watch: his record (`+0x9ad4..`) with the same competition (`+0x3f`), dates (`+0x2a`, `+0x28`), club (`+0`), `+0x34` and both sides (`+0xc`, `+0x10`). Null fixture or human out of range: the original routine runs (error box and 0).

Tells whether the human may watch the fixture: 1 when the fixture has a negative `+0x43` and neither it nor the fixtures of that day (in each key-nation group) have a club of the human; otherwise 0. \n `HUMAN_MANAGER::can_watch_fixture(partida, humano)` (fixture, human): the human (or, if null, the one of the current screen `[0xb74c26 + 0x300 × [0xb77c7a]]`) can watch the fixture if it has a negative `+0x43`, neither of the two clubs (`+0x1c`, `+0x20`, with flags `+0x40`, `+0x41`) is his (`0x600a50`) and, in each group of the key nations (`[0xb64738]`), no fixture in the list of its day (date `+0x28`/`+0x2a`, time slot `+0x3f`; `0x5ae6a0`) has a club of his. \n Null fixture: the "Error" box (`0x707`) and 0. Called by the clean-up of watched fixtures (`0x5fe8d0`) and by the choice of the fixture (`0x5fe500`).

Removes the person's nickname from every human manager: in each one, finds the nickname (30 bytes), pulls the next ones up, blanks the last one and lowers the count; then sorts the last manager's array. \n `HUMAN_MANAGER::remove_nickname_from_all(id)`: in each non-null human manager (`[this]`, `[this+4]` records of `0xa6ef` bytes; counter in a signed byte), with no nickname array (`+0xa6e3`) it exits for good; otherwise it searches (bsearch with `0x601a10`, which reads only the id at `+0`; the key has byte `+4` zeroed and the rest undefined, the port uses zero) for the nickname of person `*id` among the `[+0xa6eb]` 30-byte ones; if found: pulls the following ones up one place, the last one gets id −1 and `+4` = 0 and the count goes down. \n At the end it re-sorts (qsort) only the array of the last manager seen (with no managers, `id` stands in for the manager, as in the original).

Tells whether the current human manager runs the club (or, for second national teams, the nation's main team). \n Does the current human manager run `clube` (or, for second national teams, the nation's main national team, `0x53b3d0`)? He must be the club's manager (`+0xcf`); without `qualquer` (any), he must not have flags `+0x9ace` (`0x5fe040`) or `+0x9a01` in the human record `[0xb63c98]`; and then it is enough that `forcar` (force) is set, that the club is a national team (`0x53b900`) or flag `+0x9a05` (`0x5fd480`). Null club: the original routine runs (error box and 0).

Stores `valor` at `+0x9a65` of the human manager record (`0xa6ef` bytes). Returns 1. \n Writes `valor` (value) at `+0x9a65` of the record of human manager `tecnico` (without one, the current one at `[0xb74c26 + 0x300 × [0xb77c7a]]`) among the humans `this` (`[this]`, `0xa6ef` bytes each; the index is id − `[0xae2364]` + 16, up to `[this+4]` − 1). No manager or index out of range: the original routine runs (error box).

Turns the human manager's holiday on or off, keeping the count of humans on holiday; when turning it on, answers pending news. \n `HUMAN_MANAGER::set_on_holiday(férias, técnico)` (holiday, manager): with no manager, the current human (`[0xb74c26 + 0x300 × [0xb77c7a]]`); none: the box of line `0x41c`. The manager's index (id − `[0xae2364]` + 16) outside 0..`[this+4]`: the box of line `0x428`. The holiday flag (`+0x9a01` of the `0xa6ef`-byte record in `[this]`) becomes `férias`, with the count of humans on holiday (`+0xc`) going up when turned on and down when turned off; when turned on, the manager's pending news with the club (`+0x39`) and with the national team (`+0x24`) are answered (`0x7874b0`); with the day in `[0xb67a50]`, the day's interest (`0x6b5040`).

Returns the first row of the 35-row key nation table holding the given nation, or 4. \n `key_nation_index_of_nation(nação)` (nation): the first row of the table of the 35 key nations (`0xb63d60`, 72 bytes, nation at `+0`) with the given nation (without checking for null), or 4. Called by the match morale `0x4cb250`, the retirements `0x7a7310`, the free friendly `0x5c6b70`, the prizes of the nations' day and the UEFA places. TapeCall for every player: no counter.

Returns the key nation row of the club: the row of its chosen nation; for a national team, 1; for a nation not chosen, the row of its continent, or 3. \n `key_nation_index_of_club(clube)` (club). A club that is not a national team (`0x53b900`), with a nation (`+0x53`) chosen to be played (`+0x11c` of the nation): the nation's row in the table, or the "Error" box (line `0x26d`) and 0. Otherwise (the original calls `0x53b900` again): national team, 1; the first row whose continent (`+4`) is that of the club's nation (`+0x71`), or 3 (with no nation, 3). Called by the retirements `0x7a7310`, the weather postponement `0x923630`, the days until the season `0x59b4c0`, the desired contract `0x85fc50`, the season year `0x669950` and others. No counter.

Returns the club's season year: the previous year when today is before the season start day of its row. \n `key_nation_get_club_season_year(clube)` (club): today's year (`[0xae2c92]`); for a club that is not a national team, by the club's row (`0x669360`): with the row's dword `+0x17` not zero or the start day (`+0x15`, unsigned) below 60, and today's day (`[0xae2c90]`, signed) before the start day, the previous year. The original returns only the low 16 bits meaningfully (the high ones are left over from the pushed slot). Called by the club records `0x444930`/`0x447430`/`0x448ad0` and the player history `0x7c3e40`/`0x7c5fe0`.

By the start and end days of the club's nation row and today, tells whether the club is in season and gives the start and end dates with the right year. 
 Convention: cdecl, `key_nation.cpp`, SEH frame only for the local dates. `key_nation_club_in_season(clube, &início, &fim)` (club, &start, &end). The row of the club's nation (`+0x53`) in the table of the 35 key nations (`0xb63d60`, 72 bytes; with no nation or outside the table, row 3 `0xb63e38` and the end day of the default date `0x54a110`, 40). `a` = day `+0x2a` of the row (start), `c` = the day of date `+0x39` (end; the original also copies the next 7 bytes and, with club `+0x1db` ≠ −1 and byte `+0x43` 3, 4 or 5, swaps two of them, but does not use them), `t` today's day (`[0xae2c90]`) and `y` the year (`[0xae2c92]`); signed 16-bit comparisons. 
 With a > c (a season that crosses the year): t > a, (a, y) and (c, y+1), 1; t < c, (a, y−1) and (c, y), 1; otherwise (a, y) and (c, y), 0. With a ≤ c: t < a, (a, y) and (c, y), 0; t > c, (a, y+1) and (c, y+1), 1; otherwise (a, y) and (c, y), 1. The dates go to `início` and `fim` when not null. 
 Called by the club in season `0x547770`, the fitness `0x62a920`, `0x62c680` and `0x62ce30`, the month of the season end `0x4d45f0` and the transfer date `0x8cee70`. TapeCall for every player: no counter.

Returns the competition's key nation row: the nation's row, 0 for the World Cup, 1 for national team tournaments, 2 for the club world cups, the continent's row or 3. \n `key_nation_index_of_comp(competição)` (competition), called by the scope of the match rules `0x8d2fa0`, the league day `0x6847c0`, the cup records `0x519890` and the match key nation `0x48dd70` of cpt_3. A nation competition (`+0x5d`): its row in the table of the 35 key nations (`0xb63d60`, 72 bytes), or 4. With no nation: the World Cup and its qualifiers, 0; national team tournament (`0x669ae0`), 1; the Club World Cup and the FIFA Club World Championship, 2; otherwise the continent row (nation 0) with the competition's continent (`+0x59`), or 3. \n The original reads `+0x5d` before checking for a null competition (the error case never reaches the box). TapeCall for every match: no counter.

The end of the match day: frees the global list, the day's arrays and, for each match, the engine, the summary and the `+0x5f` object. \n Frees the global list `[0xb67dc8]`, the two day arrays (`+1`, `+0xd`) and, for each match (`+0x19`, `0x69` bytes each, `+0x21` of them), the engine (`0x6b97a0` and freed; the match leaves `[0xde2f70]` via `0x90d6b0`), the summary (`+0x5b`) and the object at `+0x5f` (`0x453bc0`); finally the match array.

Clears each of the day's matches' fields and picks the human's match (or the first marked one) for the screen. Returns 1 if there was one of the human's. \n With matches on the day (`+0x2b`), it clears the `0x40` bytes of each one (`+0xd`, `0x54` bytes, `+0x15` of them) from `+0x14` and picks the human's (`+0x10`; otherwise the first with `+0xc`) for the screen (`0x717cc0` and `0x7fc7e0` with `[0xb67a48]` on).

Starts the day's next match after the current one (`+0x2f`): skips the decided ones, those of a human club and those already started; creates the engine and prepares it; in the 1st pass with none, moves to the 2nd. Returns 1 if it started one. \n Starts the next match of the day (`+0x19`, `0x69` bytes each, `+0x21` of them) after the current one (`+0x2f`; -2 = finished). The current one still with an engine (`+0x57`): error `0x68d`. It skips those already decided (`+0x47` -2), those with no match set in the 2nd pass (`+0x33` 1 and `+0x63.+0x10` zero), those of a human club (`0x600a50` with `+0x44`/`+0x45`) and those already started (`+0x47` != -1, `+0x57`, `+0x53`). \n On the chosen one: takes it off queue `[0xde2f70]` (`0x90d2f0` with -3), creates the engine (`0xf63b` bytes, `0x6b7e50`; without it error `0x6b2` and it carries on) and prepares it (`0x6b7f20` with the fast mode from `0x6b66a0`); `+0x2f` = it, returns 1. With none: in the 1st pass (`+0x33` 1) it moves to 2 and starts again from the beginning; otherwise `+0x2f` = -2 and returns 0.

Moves the day's current match (`+0x2f`) forward: one engine step (1 in 3 or 6 calls, by the modes in `[0xae3138]`) or to the end; when it finishes, creates the summary, records it, frees the engine and takes it off the queue. Returns 1 if the match finished. \n Without `ate_o_fim` (to the end), only 1 in every 3 (`0x40000` in `[0xae3138]+4`) or 6 (`0x80000`) calls, by counter `[0xb67a54]` (0..100), and one engine step (`0x6b98c0` with 1); with `ate_o_fim`, steps (-1) to the end. The state goes to `+0x67`; on finishing (2 or 8) it counts in `+0x25`, creates the summary (`+0x5f`, `0xd7a` bytes with 2 objects of `0x625` at `+0x11f`; without it error `0x713`), records it (`0x7293f0`), frees the engine and takes the match off queue `[0xde2f70]` (`0x90d6b0`).

Closes one of the day's matches: copies the day's match into the fixture, records the result in the competition (method 1, or the away-game path) and runs the post-match: players, events, contracts, suspensions, states, the history and each side's club. \n The closing of day match `p` (`0x69` bytes): copies the `0x4f` bytes from p+4 to the fixture (`+0`) and, with a competition (`+0x14`), reads the round number of a human club (`[adadfc]` of the competition `+8`, `0x4a4850`, `+0x2d` above 1; as in the original, it looks only at the away club `+0x20` on both passes) and records the result: p+`0x47` = -3 (away game, `0x924050` with bits 12-13 of `+0x4d` and the copy with scores -1 in `0x5ab510`/`0x5aa680`) or method 1 of the competition. \n Then the post-match with the summary (p+`0x5f`): players (`0x6b6cc0`), events (`0x6b74a0`), contracts (`0x4ca6d0`), suspensions (`0x55ca00`), `0x76b600` (except for -3), states (`0x62c080`) and, except for -3, the history (`[0xb74434]` method 1, outside `[0x9cf684]`), `0x7c0d70`, `0x8c39f0`, `0x444930`, `0x868830`, `0x4134c0`, `0x6951e0`, `0x59a5d0`, `0x7f8c00` and the club of each side (`0x6b79a0` with the round). Without `p`, error `0x73f` and 0.

Plays the match day: on a network it ties the humans to their matches and plays them to the end; then plays each match without an engine; finally closes each match, redoes the humans' stored tactics and frees the summaries. Returns 1. 
 Convention: thiscall, `match_day.cpp`, ~3.3 KB. Plays day `dia` (`+0x19` matches of `0x69` bytes, `+0x21` of them, `+0x25` finished, `+0x34` the human's). It starts the next one (`0x6b5a70`). On a network (`[0xa5a390]`): for each pending match with a human (`+0x53`) it creates the humans' scoreboard (`+0x5b`, `0x11d` bytes), ties each human to his side (`0x765480` `+0xe2`/`+0xe6`, `0x4542f0`, `0x727f00`), stores the highest level (`0x5fcff0`) and passes it on (`0x5fd100`); then it notifies those not playing (`0x71b1b0`), releases the humans and plays their matches to the end. 
 Then, each match still without an engine (`+0x47` -1): with a human on a network, it moves the current one to the end (`0x6b5ce0`) and starts everything again; otherwise it creates the engine (`0x6b7e50`, `0x6b7f20`), plays to the end (`0x6b98c0` -1, counting in `+0x25`), creates the summary (`0xd7a` bytes), records it (`0x7293f0`), frees the engine and, if the engine was not in fast mode (`+0` of the engine zero), writes the score with the day's percentage on the bar (`0x66f4e0`, `0x802f80`). 
 Finally it moves the current one (`0x6b5ce0` with 1), closes each match (`0x6b5f00`), redoes the humans' stored tactics (`0x5fbe20`, `0x5fbd00`, `0x5b5960`) and frees the summaries; with a score written, the date on the bar (`0x54ba20`).

Sets up the match day (date, mode 0..2): zeroes the arrays, gathers the pending matches of each list, records the already decided ones, groups by list and by competition, points each match to its competition, creates the global list and works out the day's interest. Returns the day. 
 Sets up day `dia` with the matches of date `data` in mode `modo` (0, 1 or 2; otherwise or with no date, error `0x93`). Zeroes the day (`+0` mode; arrays `+1` groups of 24 bytes, `+0xd` competitions of `0x54`, `+0x19` matches of `0x69`, each with capacity and count; `+0x2f` -1, `+0x33` 1). 
 For each of the `[0xb64738]` lists (`0x5ae6a0`): the pending matches (`+0x43` <= -1, except -2) go into the day (copy of `0x4f` bytes; `+0x67` -1), those decided earlier (`0x923630` bit 0) are recorded and marked -2 (`0x923cc0`, `0x5ab510`/`0x5aa680`), the others notified (`0x79c7b0`); the list's group (`0x48dcd0`) stores the range of its matches, which is sorted (qsort with `0x6b6510`) and split by competition (`+4` of the copy), and each match points to its own (`+0x63`). 
 Finally the global list `[0xb67dc8]` (`0x68d020`) and the day's interest (`0x6b5040`). The arrays grow 5 at a time (`0x945667`; out of memory, errors `0xd6`, `0xf4`, `0x140`).

The current human leaves the match he was watching; with no other human watching, the match runs to the end, is recorded and leaves the queue. \n The current human (`[0xb77c7a]`) leaves the match he was watching (called only when a network player leaves, `0x838c00`). His match (`[0xb74c26 + 0x300 × turn]`, `0x765480` → `+0xe2`): if another of the 16 humans (the last 16 records of `[0xae23bc]`, 110 bytes, `+0x5f` active) watches the same one and it is his turn (`0x7fffa0` on the manager), it leaves silently; otherwise it removes the turn from the four arrays of the summary (`+0x5b`: `+5`/`+0x45`/`+0x85`/`+0xc5`, the counters `+0x105..+0x108`). \n Nobody else watching: it creates the engine (`+0x57`, `0xf63b` bytes, `0x6b7e50` + `0x6b7f20`; without it error `0xa4b`), runs to the end (`0x6b98c0` with −1; state `+0x67`, 2 or 8 count in `[[0xb67a50]+0x25]`), except for 8 creates the summary (`+0x5f`, `0xd7a` bytes with 2 objects of `0x625` at `+0x11f`; without it error `0xa68`) and records it (`0x7293f0`), frees the engine and takes the match off queue `[0xde2f70]` (`0x90d6b0`).

Finds in the fixture list the match of a statistics record (date, competition and club) and copies the fixture. Returns 1 if found. \n The fixture (`0x4f` bytes) of record `k` of the statistics index (`[this]`, 12 bytes: `+0` competition, `+4` one of the clubs, `+8`/`+0xa` the date): it asks the schedule `[0xae2a58]` (`0x5acbe0`) for the matches of that date and competition in a local list (`0x68d020`) and copies to `saida` the first one with club `+4` at home (`+0xc`) or away (`+0x10`). Index outside 0..`[this+0x1c]` or null output: the original routine runs (error box, 0).

One step of the human's match on a network, by the clock and the humans' scoreboard (everyone sees each state; sounds, events, engine step, end, half time, goals, minute); records it and picks the day's human match. Returns 1 if it changed. \n One step of human match `p` on a network, by the clock (`0x90c510`) and the humans' scoreboard (`+0x5b`: `+0` state, `+1` event, `+0x85` who has already seen it, `+0x105` humans, `+0x107` seen, `+0x108` pause, `+0x109` wait, `+0x10d` time, `+0x111` may advance, `+0x115` highlight). Without `p`, it moves the current one (`0x6b5ce0`) and starts the next (`0x6b5a70`). \n It waits for everyone to see the state; then the sounds (`0x6d8c70`) and the time; it shows the next event (`0x6d78b0`, highlight by table `0x6d5cd0`) or takes one engine step (`0x6b98c0` with 1) and sets the state: end (2/8), half time (4), goals on each side (`+0xf5bd`/`+0xf5f3` against the summary), highlight, `+0x8eb2`, the minute (`+0x8ed0` / 11) against the summary (wait `0x226` - 50 x `+0x51`); with a state, it records it (`0x729ff0`) and the day's human match (`+0x34`) becomes the one with the highest competition (`0x6b6570`) or the furthest along.

Each human confirms the network match; with all of them confirmed, creates the engine and prepares it for watching, or plays it to the end and records it. \n The current human (`[0xb77c7a]`) confirms match `p` on a network (humans' scoreboard `+0x5b`: `+0x45` who confirmed, `+0x105` humans, `+0x106` confirmed). With all: it creates the engine (`0x6b7e50`) and prepares it for watching (`0x6b7f20` with the last argument 1). If it is not one to be watched (returns 0), it plays to the end (counting in `[0xb67a50]+0x25`), creates the summary, records it (`0x7293f0`), frees the engine, takes it off the queue and sets `+0x119`; if it is, it notifies the commentator (`+0x8f7a` = 3), creates the summary, records it for watching (`0x729ff0`) and returns 1. Errors `0x4b8` (no match), `0x4d0`, `0x4ea`, `0x511` (out of memory).

Applies the squad rule (foreigners, non-EU or age) to the club's lineup: swaps restricted players for the candidates with the smallest score loss. \n Enforces squad rule `regra` (byte 0: 1 foreigner from outside the community, 2 foreigner, 3 over the age in `+1`; `+2` maximum on the pitch, `+3` maximum on the bench, `+4` and `+5` the allowed and the current) on the lineup of `clube` (nation `+0x53`; `0x53d980`/`0x53d740`): removes the restricted ones from the reserve list (`reserva`, `nr`); if there are more restricted players on the pitch than the maximum (`+2`), it chooses among the restricted starters and the candidates (non-restricted bench + reserve) via `0x6e2000` and swaps, one by one, the one with the smallest score loss (`0x6e2f20`), redoing the bench (`0x6e2000`) if a starter came from it; then it does the same on the bench (`saida` + `nt`) with the maximum `+3` (or `+4` − `+5`).

The player's score for a position outside a match (transfers and scouting): position, form, perceived ability, contract, age, scout knowledge. \n The score of player `p` for position `pos` outside the match (transfers, scouting), by the `flags`, for `clube`, with the cut-off `limite` and scout `o`: the position score (table `0xa15d50`) times the adjustment for reputation, form, perceived ability, age, contract and the scout's knowledge. -10000 with no player sheet (`+0x61`) or below the cut-off.

The player's score for a lineup slot: like the off-match score, plus the second position, in-match condition, tactics, veterans and holidays. \n The score of player `p` (player sheet `f`) for a lineup slot (`pos`, and the second position `pos2` with weight 1/3), by the `flags`, at `clube`, with side `lado` (`+0x1b` scout, `+0x1f` knowledge), manager `tecnico`, the `limite` (cut-off), the tactic flags (`marca` and `bytes`, `tatica`) and the holiday list `ferias` (16 pairs of id, position). Like `0x6e6340` (table `0xa15cfc`), plus the condition in the match (`reg`, the player in the match), the tactic, the veterans' age and the holiday bonus. -10000 with no person or player sheet; -1000000 if vetoed.

A player's current or potential ability as an observer sees it (reputation, noise and the observer's knowledge). \n The ability of player `p` (2 = current, otherwise potential) as observer `o` (0 = the manager of club `c`, `+0xcf`) sees it: the reputation `rep` (negative: via `0x5407e0`) / 50 mixes with the true ability (player sheet `+0x61`: `+5` current, `+7` potential) and a pseudo-random noise (player id + `[0xdd7120]` + observer id) that shrinks with the observer's knowledge (`0x544410` of sheet `+0x69`, levels `+0x17`/`+0x18`, up to 20). With the observer's sheet, high knowledge and a favourable seed, the exact current ability.

Stores the extreme players of each side among the active ones (position >= 0 and, in 0..=10, `table_a` different from 1): side 0, smallest y at `0xf58e` and largest at `0xf596`; side 1, largest y at `0xf592` and smallest at `0xf59a`. With no candidate the previous value stays. \n Convention: `match_eng.cpp`.

The player takes the ball: releases the previous owner's, credits the pass (counter and disposition by zone), records possession and the ball on his square. \n It releases the previous owner's ball (`0xf582`, the same writes as `release_ball`), clears the play state, credits the pass (`0xf576`, same side: counter `0x2` and disposition + `0x6c`/`0x60`/`0x96`/`0x78` according to role and zone), records the new owner, the ball on his square, the side in possession (`0x1a5` + side) and the possession count (`0x8d46` + side). The engine is re-read on every access, as in the original.

The constructor of the match statistics: checks for the CM01/02 CD and builds the statistics: loads from the save or creates the index, the buckets and the zeroed temporary file. Returns `this`. \n It checks the CD: among the drives (GetLogicalDriveStringsA, 200) the first CD drive (GetDriveTypeA 5) with "<root>cm0102.exe" (`0x4c0aa0`; on the others it closes the search, `0x4c0c10`); without it, the "Insert CD" box and it tries again, forever. \n With `zip` and the save loaded (`0x72aa80`), done; otherwise the index of `n` entries (`+4`, `[this]` with n × 12 bytes; out of memory, error `0x62` and the game closes), `+0x1c` = n, the four bucket cursors (`+8`: k × n / 4) and "match_stats_matches.tmp" (CM3_TEMP, "wb") with `n` zeroed records of `0xd7a` bytes (error `0x71` if it cannot open, `0x7e` if the write fails), `+0x18` = 0. The local record is created and destroyed by the runtime's vector iterators (`0x9463af`/`0x9462bb`) as in the original.

Fills the match statistics record: clubs, dates, attendance, gate receipts, weather, sorted events, formation, captain and the 20 players of each side. Returns 1. \n Convention: thiscall, ret `0xc`, `match_stats.cpp`; `this` is not used. Fills statistics record `reg` of match `m` (fixture in `[m+0x4792]`): clubs, dates, attendance (`+0x34`) and gate receipts (`+0x38`, `0x59af40` only without `sem_renda` (no receipts)), the score by half, the stadium, the referee, the minute / 11, the weather (`0x923010` at `+0xd76`), up to 50 events of 4 bytes at `+0x57` (sorted by `0x72b160`, terminated by `0xff`) and, per team (`+0x11f` + `0x625` × t), the statistics, the formation (`0x5b2ae0`), the captain (`0x897590` with `sem_renda`) and the 20 players of `0x49` bytes (shirt number via `0x85a760`, assigning one with `0x85a470` when missing). Null match or record: the original routine runs (error box).

qsort comparer of the 4-byte match events: orders two events by type group, then by minute and arrival order. \n Same group (types 1..3 together, 7..8 together, or the same type +2): tie broken by the minute (`+3`, unsigned) and then by arrival order (`+0` signed, half); different groups: the difference of the types.

Builds the live match screen: team headers and score, commentary, clock, control, tactics buttons, commentary speeds, tabs, the selected tab panel, the stadium and the commentary panel. 
 Convention: cdecl, SEH, `match_screens.cpp`, ~5 KB. It sets flag `+0xea` of the human's record (`0x765480`) and frees the snapshot of param `0x1d`. Mode 1 (param 1): only the empty background figure (`0x41c0d0`). 
 Otherwise: it removes the "left" mark (−911) of the human among the spectators (`[partida+0x5b]` `+0xc5` + 4h, counting in `+0x108`); the background; the headers of the two teams (kit colours `0x53b640`, name, club box, score or "A" for abandoned) and the aggregate (`[+0x4f]` ≥ 0; added to the score outside mode 2 of `[+0x67]`); the commentary area (background "match.mbr"), the clock area (minute `[+0x4d]` in param 3), the "<<<"/">>>" arrows (or the symbols of font `[0x9cc2c4]`), the control (`0x725a70`, param 4) and the tactics buttons of both teams (params 5 and 6; the one in param `0x15` marked); with the human in charge of one of the teams (`0x600c90`) or with no human at all (`0x600a50`), the commentary speeds (`0x5fcff0`; the current one marked, focus `[Display+0x12f4ff]` and the commentator volume `[+0x2db0]`). 
 Finally record `+0` = 3, the tabs (Overview, Stats, Zones, Report, the team statistics, Ratings, Latest Scores and, for a real league without national teams, League Table), −1 in param 8, the tab panel (param 2), the stadium and, with param 8 at −1, the commentary panel (with the highlight of param 7 narrated by `0x6d7b00`) in param 8.

Handles input on the live match screen for item `item` (−1: the passing of time): commentary volume and speed, the new event (clock, commentary, modes), watching or not, a team's tactics, switching tabs and each tab's input. 
 On a network (`[0xb77c84]`) or with the match to be confirmed in mode 1 without confirmation: 0; spectators closed (`[+0x119]`): −9; mode 1: confirms over the network (`0x6b5260`) and, once confirmed, moves to mode 2 and −11. The item with id `0xc` changes the commentator volume (`[+0x2db0]`); a volume different from the manager's speed (`0x5fcff0`) passes it on (`0x5fd100`) and −11. 
 No item: with the human connected (`0x5fd210`), modes 2 and 3 become 4 (stops watching) and 5 stops the commentary (`0x802a50`, −9); in mode 4 with a new event (`0x6b55c0`) it reads the match menu flags (`+0`: 1 and 2 redo everything, 4 the clock, 8 narrates the highlight (`0x6d7b00`) and, on substitution ones, marks the human's team in param `0x15`, `0x20` and `0x40` modes 3 and 5); the "waiting" flag (param `0x24`) and the control label (`0x725a70`); with no team marked, it looks for the human's (params `0x2f`/`0x30`). 
 With a team to open (the marked one, or the item with id 1): opens its tactics (`0x899a50`, −4) if the match allows it (`[+0x8eb2]` with no highlight), otherwise re-marks the buttons (`0x800d30`) and param `0x15`. Item id 2: watch or not (modes 2/3/4), 5 stops (−9); id 3: changes the tab (param 2). The menu bar (`0x7643d0`; −4 marks the human as leaving, −911) and then the tab decides (the panels `0x71d9e0`, `0x71e750`, `0x720320` (id 4 changes the period of param `0xa`), `0x723350`; the handlers `0x722dc0` and `0x725860`; tab 10 converts param `0x26` into `0x25`). Finally −11 with `[0xb6b7b0]` or the redraw (`0x802d00`) with `[0xb6b7a8]`.

Builds the details screen of a stored match: loads the match record and snapshot from the match stats, the team headers, the 7 tabs and the selected tab panel. \n Convention: cdecl, SEH, `match_screens.cpp`. It frees the snapshot of param `0x1d`; without the record (param `0x1f`) it reads that of the match in param `0x1e` from the statistics (`0x729e30`, `0x4f` bytes) and without the snapshot (`0x20`) it builds it (`0x729600`, `0xd7a` bytes; on error: "Error" box and nothing more); the background, the headers of the two teams (colours `0x53b640`, name, club box, score or "Match Abandoned"), the aggregate (`[+0x4b]` ≥ 0), the menu bar, the 7 tabs, the back and forward buttons and the tab panel (param 2).

Redraws the overview possession bar when the share changes (percentages and the colour of the club with more of the ball) and stores the match state in the param `0x1d` copy. \n In the match (param 0), with no penalty shoot-out (`[estado + 0x53]` = 0), it takes the colours of the two clubs (`0x53b640` with kits `+0x152` and `+0x777`) and, if possession (`+0x142`) changed since the copy in param `0x1d` (or there is no copy), it redraws the overview possession bar: the percentage (50 with no value or without flag `+0x767`) as "%d%%" in items 3 and 4 from param `0x21`, split from `0x115` to `0x2c9` at the height of param `0x22`, and the colour of the club with more possession in item 5. At the end it stores the state in the copy (which is created here if it does not exist).

Draws the match overview from `*topo` to `*base` (`*base` −= `0x28` right away): period, possession bar and commentary, date, score with half time/extra time/penalties, competition, scorers and cards, shoot-out, referee, attendance, weather and abandoned match. \n Convention: cdecl, `match_screens.cpp`, ~6 KB. In the match (param 0; state at `+0x5f`): the period title (by `[estado + 0x4f]`, with the names of param 1 = 4 or the others) and, with no penalty shoot-out (`[estado + 0x53]` = 0), the possession bar (frame, "Last 5 Mins", the club colours; the item in param `0x21`, the height in `0x22`; `*base` −= `0x37`) and the commentary box (with param 7 the commentator writes the last highlight in it, `0x6d7b00`; the item in param 8). Outside the match: the stadium and the city of param `0x1f`, with the state of param `0x20`. \n Then: the date, the score (`0x4bf930`) with half time, extra time and penalties, the competition (with shortcut `0x7e5` when it is neither a friendly nor a national team one), the list of scorers in two columns (goals, own goal, missed penalty, sending off, injury; the minutes of the same player and type together, breaking the line with more than 10 letters), the penalty shoot-out, the referee, the attendance, the weather, "Match Abandoned" and the possession bar (`0x71d9e0`).

Draws the live league table (league, top, bottom) on a copy of the league with the day's scores applied (or the draw date notice): title, headers, separators, position, up/down arrow, club and columns. \n Convention: cdecl, `match_screens.cpp`, ~3.4 KB; the map says `(void)`, but the original reads three arguments: the league, `topo` and `base`, by value. It makes a local copy of the league (League `0x682200` + `0x682380`, the temporary destroyed with `0x682300`) and, in the match with live scores (`[[p0+0x57]+0x8ed0]`), applies to it (`0x685f60`) the day's matches of the group in param `0xe` of its competition: the human's match with the score from the state (`+0x11f`/`+0x744`, penalties `+0x120`/`+0x745`), the others with no result yet as 0-0, those that already have a score by the count up to the minute (`0x728e90`); sorts the copy. \n With the draw date (`[liga+0xb6]`, `[+0xb8]`+`[+0x40]`) still to come: only the competition name and "The draw will be made on ..." (`0x5ed070`). Otherwise: the title, the 11-column table (the rows by the promotion and relegation places or by the space), the headers, the league with `[+0xad]` = param `0x28` sorted (`0x6827d0`) for the position arrows, one row per club (separators `0x6400`, position, up/down arrow, name with shortcut `0x7d5` and the human's colour, and the record columns by param `0x28`), the scrolling (param `0x25`) and the table item in `0x26`. No league or no param `0xe` ("Error" box): the original routine runs.

Draws the team selection check for the club (param 0), the match (param 1) and the squad (param 2): warns (with linked names) about players on international duty, on loan, unavailable, ineligible, banned, injured or without a work permit, the bench limit or missing starters; otherwise asks for confirmation (captain, set piece takers, substitutes) with "No" and "Yes". \n Convention: cdecl, `match_screens.cpp`, ~7 KB with the pieces up to `0x727c2e`. It goes through the 20 slots of the tactic (`0x8968f0`): counts starters (< 11), substitutes (< 11 + the bench `[jogo+0x4d]` & `0xf`) and those left out; of those in the team, it gathers those called up by the national team (`0x7757d0`), those loaned to another club (`0x4cf6d0`/`0x4cf5a0`, outside the national team), the ineligible ones with the same reason as the first (`0x8cf5e0`), the suspended (`0x55d270`), the injured and the unavailable (`0x62c400`/`0x62ed70`: an injury of type `0x4d` to `0x51` in language 0 counts as unavailable) and those without a work permit (`0x8c7560`, outside competition `[0x9cf684]` and friendlies). \n Then the club background, the menu, the colours and the title with the name. The first non-empty group, in that order, becomes the "Team Selection" warning with the (linked) names and the "Ok" button; otherwise the day's bench limit (`0x8cf880`); otherwise fewer than 11 starters; otherwise "Please Confirm": the chosen captain (`0x727e20`) when there is no valid one, the set piece takers outside the 11, the missing substitutes, those outside the squad, "Proceed to the match ?" and the list with "No" and "Yes".

Reads the record index, the four bucket cursors and the counts from `match_stats.dat` in the saved game. Returns 1 if it read. \n Reads from the save's "match_stats.dat" (`0x9326e0` in zip `zip`) the count at `+4`, the index (12 bytes each, allocated in `[this]`), the four bucket cursors (`+8`), `+0x1c` and `+0x18`. Null zip: the original routine runs (error box). No file: error `0x49e`; read or allocation failure: error `0x4a5`/`0x4ae`/`0x4b6`/`0x4be`/`0x4c6`/`0x4ce` and it closes.

Writes the record index, the four bucket cursors and the counts to `match_stats.dat` in the saved game. Returns 1 if it wrote. \n Writes to the save's "match_stats.dat" (`0x9326e0` for writing) the count (`+4`), the index `[this]`, the four cursors (`+8`), `+0x1c` and `+0x18`. Null zip: the original routine runs (error box); if it cannot open, the game stops (error `0x4f1`); write failure: error `0x4f8`/`0x500`/`0x508`/`0x510`/`0x518` and it closes.

Reads one match statistics record (`0xd7a` bytes) from `match_stats_matches.tmp` by index. Returns 1 if it read. \n Reads record `k` (`0xd7a` bytes, at position k × `0xd7a`) of "match_stats_matches.tmp" (CM3_TEMP, "rb") into `saida`. Index −1: returns 0 silently; outside 0..`[this+0x1c]` or null output: the original routine runs (error box). Cannot open: error `0x128`; fseek or fread fail: error `0x12f`/`0x137` and it closes.

Records a finished match: fills its record and writes it, except for excluded matches. Returns 1. \n Records finished match `m`: fills record `r` (`0x729ff0`, without skipping the gate receipts) and, except for a match of competition `[0x9cf684]` with `+0x4c` in the record, writes it (`0x729820`) with fixture `[m+0x4792]` and events `[m+0x8f7a]`. Null match or record: the original routine runs (error box, returns 0).

Writes the events and the record into the fixture's slot (or the bucket cursor's slot, which wraps around) and updates the index. Returns 1. \n Writes record `r` of fixture `jogo` to "match_stats_matches.tmp" ("r+b"): zeroes the 13 bytes from `+0xd69`, writes the events (`0x6d98b0` of `eventos`, human if one of the clubs `+0x1c`/`+0x20` is human-managed, `0x600a50`) and writes the record into slot `[jogo+8]`; with no slot (−1), into the slot of the bucket cursor (`0x729bd0`) at `[this+8+4b]`, which advances and goes back to the start of the bucket on reaching its end ((b+1) × `[this+0x1c]` / 4). \n At the end, entry `[jogo+8]` of the index (12 bytes in `[this]`) receives `+0xc`, `+0x10` and the dates `+0x2a`/`+0x28`. Null argument: the original routine runs (error box). File failures: error `0x172`/`0x17f`/`0x18d`/`0x1a3` (closing, as the original does).

Writes the 20 player rows of the team stats table of side `[param 0x1b]` (22 columns from the param `0x1c` table), building the cells or updating what changed. \n Convention: cdecl, `match_screens.cpp`, ~4.2 KB. Data: in the match `[p0 + 0x5f]` and p0 + 4, outside it params `0x20` and `0x1f`; row i at data + 1573·side + 73·i, empty with `0xfb` at `+0x1ad`. The 22 columns come from the table of param `0x1c` (1: `0xa16178`, 2: `0xa1618c`): number (or i + 1), two markers, the name ("(c)" for the captain; button `0x7dc`/`0x7d7` when the person checks out, `0x53e990`), the event (injury, sending off, coming on, going off) and the numbers. \n With param `0x1d` (the previous snapshot), an unchanged cell gets no text. `modo` ≠ 0 builds the cells in list `area` (`0x8040a0` button, `0x804100` text; the first item in param `0x1a` if it is at −1); `modo` 0 updates the items from param `0x1a` (`0x801c70`, `0x800d30`, `0x801960`). Param `0x1c` other than 1 and 2 (the original reads the table with no value): the original routine runs.

Rewrites the latest scores rows in pages: stage, fixture, score, period, event scorers, aggregate and the page footer. \n Convention: cdecl, `match_screens.cpp`, ~4.9 KB. Params: 0 the match or null, `0xe` the day's entry, `0xf` how many rows, `0x10` the first item, 6 items per row, `0x11` the page shown, `0x12` paused. It clears the rows, then splits the entry's matches (`[+4]` to `[+8]`, 105 bytes in `[[0xb67a50]+0x19]`) into pages (`0x13` = how many): per match the stage header (`0x4bffc0`, when it changes), the fixture row (teams, score counted from the events, period `0x6b6570`) and the event scorers (goal, penalty, own goal, missed penalty, sending off, injury; minutes of the same player together) and the aggregate. Only the page shown is written (second pass). In the footer "<< Page x/y >>" (or "Hold") with more than one page; at the end the time in param `0x14`.
